full_name: OECD.AI Policy Observatory / Global Partnership on AI (GPAI)
mission: The OECD's AI hub helps governments put the OECD AI Principles — the first intergovernmental AI standard — into practice. It tracks 900+ national AI policies, monitors AI incidents reported in the press, runs the G7 Hiroshima AI Process reporting framework for AI developers, and hosts GPAI's expert community.

key_work.title: OECD AI Principles (updated 2024)
key_work.plain_summary: The first intergovernmental AI standard (2019); the 2024 update added stronger focus on safety, privacy, intellectual property and information integrity. Endorsed by 47 jurisdictions.

key_work.title: AI Incidents and Hazards Monitor (AIM)
key_work.plain_summary: Automatically collects and classifies AI incidents and hazards reported in news worldwide, using OECD definitions.

key_work.title: Towards a common reporting framework for AI incidents
key_work.plain_summary: 29 criteria countries can use to report AI incidents in a comparable way; approved by 44 GPAI countries.

key_work.title: Hiroshima AI Process Reporting Framework 2.0
key_work.plain_summary: The only international framework for organisations to report how they manage AI risks; v2.0 (May 2026) broadens participation and covers agentic AI.

key_work.title: OECD AI Capability Indicators (beta)
key_work.plain_summary: Indicators that compare AI capabilities against human abilities across domains.

status_note: OECD.AI launched Feb 2020 to support the 2019 OECD AI Principles (updated May 2024); GPAI and OECD AI work merged into an integrated partnership under the GPAI brand in July 2024.

warnings.text: AI incidents and hazards are rising and need consistent tracking across countries.
General-purpose and generative AI raise new challenges for safety, privacy, IP and information integrity.

recommendations.text: Governments should adopt the OECD AI Principles and common definitions of AI incidents.
AI developers should publicly report risk-management practices through the Hiroshima reporting framework.
Use interoperable tools and metrics for trustworthy AI.
